props.raw: Software Development using AI

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools

Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

props.summary: The course explores how AI-powered tools—IDEs, terminals, code review and testing platforms—are reshaping the software development life cycle. It connects core principles of building complex systems with hands-on experience using state-of-the-art AI tools, delivered through real-world engineering tasks and a team-based project guided by industry practitioners.

props.course_title: AI-Augmented Research and Development: Foundations and Practice
props.summary: This graduate-level course teaches students how to integrate AI tools into scientific research with rigor, treating large language models and prompting as an engineering discipline. It covers retrieval-augmented generation, AI-assisted software development, agentic systems, human-AI collaboration, and evaluation frameworks, culminating in a capstone project. [EXTERNAL]
topics: evaluation frameworks for detecting and analyzing Al failures

props.summary: This NUS module introduces students to generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools and their impact across diverse domains. It equips learners to use curated GAI tools effectively in academic and professional contexts while critically examining associated societal challenges. The course emphasizes practical engagement with these tools through discussions and projects.

The course provides conceptual and analytical tools for systematic software development, emphasizing object‑oriented analysis, modelling, design, implementation and testing. It teaches UML, program specification and testing methods, and discusses modularisation, correctness and software quality.
